reference_sql:
SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(l.order_line_id) AS n_lines
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-07 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-08 00:00:00'
GROUP BY o.order_id
alternatives: SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(l.order_line_id) AS n_lines FROM order_lines l RIGHT JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-07 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-08 00:00:00' GROUP BY o.order_id

SELECT o.order_id, SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_line_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS n_lines FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-07' GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_line_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS n_lines FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-07' GROUP BY 1
other_way.tradeoff: Adding 1 per matched line with CASE counts the same, but COUNT of a right-table column says it in fewer words.
